anthropicTools.name: ui_look
anthropicTools.description: See what is on the user's screen now: the route, and the tree of controls (each with an id — and a key when the app gives one — what it is, what it shows, its state and the ops it allows). picture: true also gives a picture of the screen, for what the tree can't say (images, layout, colors) — when the app can take one.

picture.description: Also a picture of the screen

anthropicTools.name: ui_act
anthropicTools.description: Do an op on a control by its id or key: e.g. read a field or a page's text, write into a field, press a button, toggle a switch, pick an option. Ops marked deny are for the user only; confirm ones wait for their yes. A page or dialog node marked behind is under what shows (another page, a dialog): its controls still work, but the user does not see them act — when they are watching, go to that page first unless it is a small aside. A container (many of the same thing: a mail list, a thread's messages) shows only a preview of its entries, not their controls: fetch one with its op "item" (args: id, or index, or query) and the answer is that entry as a tree of its own, with ids and keys to act on next (e.g. item {id: "42"} on mail.list → mail.list[42].reply). "items" pages through all its entries' keys and names. An entry's key — container key + [id], controls in it under that, mail.list[42].reply — can also be acted on straight away, even off screen: it is fetched (scrolled to) first. scroll_to / scroll move the container.

node.description: The control's id or key from the tree

anthropicTools.name: ui_tool
anthropicTools.description: Run one of the app's own tools (listed with the tree).

anthropicTools.name: ui_navigate
anthropicTools.description: Take the user to a route of the app (listed with the tree, filling in its :params), or "back". The answer is the new page's tree.

anthropicTools.name: ui_peek
anthropicTools.description: See another page's controls without taking the user there, to plan: what is on it and the keys to act on after navigating (e.g. peek /settings/ai, then navigate there and act by key). Says whether it is current or as last seen.

A page or dialog node marked behind is under what shows (another page, a dialog): its controls still work, but the user does not see them act — when they are watching, go to that page first unless it is a small aside. A container (many of the same thing: a mail list, a thread's messages) shows only a preview of its entries, not their controls: fetch one with its op "item" (args: id, or index, or query) and the answer is that entry as a tree of its own, with ids and keys to act on next (e.g. item {id: "42"} on mail.list → mail.list[42].reply). "items" pages through all its entries' keys and names. An entry's key — container key + [id], controls in it under that, mail.list[42].reply — can also be acted on straight away, even off screen: it is fetched (scrolled to) first. scroll_to / scroll move the container.

node.description: The control's id or key from the tree

openaiResponsesTools.name: ui_tool
openaiResponsesTools.description: Run one of the app's own tools (listed with the tree).

openaiResponsesTools.name: ui_navigate
openaiResponsesTools.description: Take the user to a route of the app (listed with the tree, filling in its :params), or "back". The answer is the new page's tree.

openaiResponsesTools.name: ui_peek
openaiResponsesTools.description: See another page's controls without taking the user there, to plan: what is on it and the keys to act on after navigating (e.g. peek /settings/ai, then navigate there and act by key). Says whether it is current or as last seen.

tools.name: ui_look
tools.description: See what is on the user's screen now: the route, and the tree of controls (each with an id — and a key when the app gives one — what it is, what it shows, its state and the ops it allows). picture: true also gives a picture of the screen, for what the tree can't say (images, layout, colors) — when the app can take one.

picture.description: Also a picture of the screen

content.text:
Route: /mail/inbox = /mail/:box (box=inbox)
Routes:
  /mail/:box — A mailbox; :box ∈ {inbox, archive} (which)
  /message/:id — One mail
  /reply/:id — Writing a reply
  /drafts — The drafts
Tools: set_theme — Switch the theme; empty_trash(confirm) — Delete the trash for good
[app] app "Mail" — read
  [w1] heading "Inbox"
  [w2 key=mail.search] textbox "Search" (length: 0) — Words to look for — read, write, append, clear
  [w3 key=mail.list] container "Inbox" (list) 312 entries, showing 0–2 (entry keys: mail.list[<id>]) — read, item, items, scroll_to, scroll
    · [mail.list[42]] #0 "Lunch on Tuesday?" — Wang · 10:15
    · [mail.list[41]] #1 "Invoice \"October\""
    · [40] #2 "Weekly sync"
    · … 309 more; op item fetches an entry's controls, items pages through them
  [w4 key=mail.compose] button "Compose" — press
  [w5] switch "Notify me" (checked) — toggle, set
  [w6] textbox "Password" (filled) — read(deny), write(deny)

(A picture of the screen is attached.)
